drafted_from: tool:read-a-list-view row in tool-rows.json, do-work/read-list-view.mjs, read-data/list-view.mjs and test/read-a-list-view.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Refresh my chores list from its recipes folder source, then read me the first page of it." It runs the list reader on your computer with your door config and shows the rows as a table.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: it reads or refreshes whichever list or saved view you give it by id through your door config.
instructions: 1. Have a door config file (JSON with the door, its key and names) for your own account; the README of tools/read-a-list-view describes its keys.

2. To see rows, say "Read my <list>" (or a saved view): your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs `node tools/read-a-list-view/do-work/read-list-view.mjs --config door.json --list <id> --limit 20` from the Workshop checkout, adding --after with the previous page's next.

3. To pull a list's row sources (a folder of documents, for one) into its records, say "Refresh my <list>"; it runs the same script with --refresh <id>, the only thing that runs the source tools, and writes only the rows that changed.

4. Read the JSON answer: a page is {list, fields, rows: [{id, record_id, values, title, source?}], next, complete}; a refresh is {list, sources: [{source, rows, written, removed, unchanged, refused}]}. Read next until it is null when you want every row; exit 2 puts the reason on standard error.

worked_examples.title: Refreshing a bakery's chores list from a folder of four recipes
worked_examples.ask: Refresh my chores list from its recipes source.
worked_examples.given: From tools/read-a-list-view/test/read-a-list-view.test.mjs: the command line is `node tools/read-a-list-view/do-work/read-list-view.mjs --config door.json --refresh chores`. The account has list chores (row type chore, fields chore and minutes) with one row source {source: documents, of: /recipes}, two rows of its own (sweep, mop), and a recipes folder of four documents: bread (40 minutes), buns (25), scones (15), tart (55).
worked_examples.hands_back: One JSON line {"list": "chores", "sources": [{"source": "documents", "rows": 4, "written": 4, "removed": 0, "unchanged": 0, "refused": []}]}. The rows are now records of the list with ids like documents~%2Fbread.md (its values "note.chore": "bake bread", "note.minutes": 40); sweep and mop are untouched. Refreshing again after the folder changes bread to 45 minutes and drops tart answers rows 3, written 1, removed 1, unchanged 2.
